Subject: Discount eligibility ahead of SOC 2 (FinCorp / Redwood)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our technical and procurement teams are aligned on Redwood for hosted API usage, and Procurement asked me to clarify one sticking point around the commit/volume discount.

Short version: our procurement timeline expects a signed DPA before commercial terms are finalized, but our security org cannot produce SOC 2 evidence for another 6 weeks due to their quarterly audit window. Is there a mechanism for receiving a commit tier or partial per-token discount that is contingent on DPA signature now and SOC 2 evidence delivered later?

What we'd like to understand:
- Whether a customer can sign a commit (and reserve a tiered per-token price) before SOC 2 is in our files
- If Redwood can offer an interim (partial) discount while SOC 2 attestation is pending, and what conditions you’d need (DPA signed, timeline for SOC 2 delivery, remediation steps if SOC 2 scope differs)

CC'ing procurement inbox so the team has the thread. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Jules Martin
Head of Platform Partnerships
FinCorp Payments
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discount eligibility ahead of SOC 2 (FinCorp / Redwood)

Hi Jules — thanks, and great to meet you on the call.

Short answer: yes, we can structure a conditional commit that starts on DPA signature with a staged pricing path tied to SOC 2 evidence. We have a couple of common patterns depending on how fast you can deliver SOC 2:

1) Conditional early-tier: DPA signed -> commit effective (tiered per-token pricing applied at a reduced, provisional rate). Full (final) tier requires SOC 2 report within X days. If SOC 2 not provided by deadline, pricing reverts or a reconciliation applies.

2) Holdback/escrow approach: DPA signed and a smaller upfront credit applied; once SOC 2 is provided, the remainder of the discount is released.

To give concrete options I need a couple of items from you:
- Exact target commit (USD / 12mo) or expected monthly token consumption range
- Expected date you'll have a SOC 2 report or SOC 2 checklist/evidence (you mentioned ~6 weeks)
- Whether procurement can sign the DPA now and accept a short mutual action plan to deliver SOC 2 artifacts later

Looping in Ben (AE) and Marissa (legal) so we can put language around conditional pricing and DPA timelines. Ben — can you confirm the commercial fallback language we usually use and an example provisional discount for a mid-market commit (~$150k ARR) so we can model this? Marissa — if DPA is signed before SOC 2, what minimal warranty/controls do you need documented to accept a staged price?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference

Kimberly, Ben, Marissa — thanks for the quick reply.

Answers below:
- Target commit: We're looking at a 12-month commitment in the $120k–$180k ARR range depending on final per-token price; monthly run-rate right now is small but expected to ramp.
- SOC 2 timing: our security team says a final SOC 2 report (Type II) will be available in ~6 weeks; however they can provide our SOC 2 scope summary and recent control evidence within 10 business days.
- DPA: Procurement can sign a standard DPA now (they said yes in principle) and would prefer any commercial precondition to be explicit and timeboxed.

If it helps, procurement suggested this compromise: sign DPA now, Redwood applies a provisional 10% volume discount for the first 90 days of the commitment; if SOC 2 Type II is produced within 45 days then the discounted rate is made permanent for the term. If SOC 2 is not provided within 45 days, the initial discount is reconciled (we pay the difference) or the contract moves to the next best available tier.

Would Redwood consider something like that? Also attaching the SOC 2 scope summary and a first-pass DPA redline for your legal team.

Attachments: fincorp_soc2_scope_summary.pdf, proposed_dpa_redlines.docx

Regards,
Jules
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discount eligibility ahead of SOC 2 (FinCorp / Redwood)

Hi Jules — appreciate the specificity, that helps a lot.

We can do a commercial structure close to what you suggested with these guardrails we typically use:
- DPA must be executed and effective at T0 (start date of commit).
- Provisional discount: 10% off the committed per-token unit price for the first 90 days.
- SOC 2 evidence window: client must provide SOC 2 Type II or equivalent evidence within 45 calendar days of T0 for the provisional discount to be converted to the contracted tier for the full term.
- Reconciliation: if SOC 2 not provided by day 45, Redwood reserves the right to invoice the difference between provisional and contracted pricing for the 90-day provisional period, or to reduce the remaining term pricing to the next available tier (client's choice).
- If SOC 2 is provided but scope materially differs from the SOC 2 scope summary provided, we will engage a 14-day remediation discussion to determine whether additional controls/clauses are required; commercial terms may be adjusted accordingly.

Marissa — please confirm whether legal is comfortable with the above mechanics and whether we need an additional minimal controls attestation as part of the DPA.

Jules — if that framework works, we can produce redline language for the SOW and DPA (conditional pricing addendum) and circulate for signature. Once signed, we'll set up a mutual action plan with CS to capture milestones: DPA signed, SOC 2 evidence uploaded, final reconciliation.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
